method.cold: vm.cool on FundConfig, Safe, NAV proxy, Morpho/Aave/Curve adapters, USDC, CRV (and vaults/gauge declared); feeds not cooled. First read in the test.
method.production: getAccountNav(account, address(0)) on a fresh fork per account; cold = first call, warm = repeat.
method.quote: USDC for fundNav; USD (address(0)) for getAccountNav

cold.note: N=1 cold is a first-touch outlier and is excluded

crvControl.conclusion: A +1 day warp stales the USDC path too, so the held-CRV result does not isolate CRV. The staleness is time-driven (24h-heartbeat feeds). Findings-curve-crv.md section 2 is consistent with that but not confirmed as CRV-specific.

sync.basis: fundNav cold, Morpho-type zero-balance positions (fit, N>=2); warm ceiling 213
why: Per-tx cost is the cold read; warm figures apply only within one tx after the first read.
Subscription tx needs headroom above NAV for the mint/deposit path and the 16,777,216 cap.
Production accounts 2, 9, 10 already exceed the cap cold at 26.5M.

async.basis: one NAV per settlement tx, amortized over the batch; same ceiling as sync
why: Batching cuts per-request gas, not the per-tx ceiling; the settlement tx must still fit.
Needed when user-paid sync NAV gas per subscription is too high, not when the cap binds.
Keeper/oracle update txs are paid on a cadence, on top of NAV computation (off-chain or on-chain to post).
Price is as old as the last push, which opens NAV-timing arbitrage; bound it with staleness checks.
Fallback when the cap binds: a pushed snapshot avoids the single-tx limit for large accounts.
